title: OutOfMemory Error: Heap Exhaustion in Globex Services
text:
Symptom: Globex microservice crashes with 'java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space' or Python process killed with 'MemoryError' / OS OOM killer log entry ('Out of memory: Kill process <PID>'). Kubernetes pod restarts with OOMKilled reason.

Root Cause: JVM or Python process heap limit too low for current data volume; unbounded in-memory cache growing during high-traffic periods; large dataset loaded fully into memory instead of streamed.

Diagnosis Steps:
1. Run 'kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n globex-prod' — look for 'OOMKilled' in Last State
2. Check pod memory usage: 'kubectl top pod <pod-name> -n globex-prod'
3. For Java: review GC logs, enable with -Xlog:gc*:file=/var/log/gc.log
4. For Python: use memory_profiler or tracemalloc to identify large allocations

Fix:
- Java: increase heap -Xmx4g in Globex Helm values: globex-services/helm/values.yaml under jvmOptions
- Python: increase pod memory limit in Kubernetes: resources.limits.memory: 2Gi
- Fix unbounded cache: add TTL and max-size to Globex CacheManager (see internal wiki: Cache Configuration)
- Stream large datasets instead of loading fully: use pandas read_csv(chunksize=10000) or Java streaming APIs
- Globex-specific: check the ReportGenerationJob — it accumulates report rows in memory; use temp DB tables

Prevention: Set Kubernetes resource requests and limits; configure HPA to scale before OOM; alert on memory > 85%.
